### `.github/workflows/fpl_logger.yml`

_108 lines_

```yaml
name: Continuous Learning Engine

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * *'  # Nightly bootstrap archive
    - cron: '0 16 * * 5' # Friday Snapshot
    - cron: '0 10 * * 2' # Tuesday Ingest
    - cron: '0 10 * * 3' # Wednesday Auto-Tune
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      step:
        description: 'Which step to run manually'
        required: true
        default: archive
        type: choice
        options: [archive, snapshot, ingest, autotune]

permissions:
  contents: write # Crucial for auto-committing weights.json

jobs:
  run_pipeline:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # requirements.txt pins numpy>=2.4,<3 (Stage 8a), and numpy 2.3+ requires
      # Python >=3.11 -- pip has no way to see that from a 3.10 interpreter,
      # so it silently narrows the candidate list to <=2.2.6 and then fails
      # with "no matching distribution" against the >=2.4 floor. tests.yml
      # already runs 3.11 against the same requirements.txt; this just
      # matches it so both workflows install the identical dependency set
      # instead of drifting again.
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'

      # Was a hand-maintained list (requests pulp pandas psycopg2-binary
      # numpy), which had already drifted twice: `pandas` was in there used
      # nowhere in the repository, silently supplying python-dateutil (which
      # fpl_tools imports unguarded) as a side effect, and `scipy` -- which
      # fpl_tools._devig_power needs for its power-method de-vig solver --
      # was missing outright, so every scheduled job silently ran the
      # proportional-split fallback instead of the real one. Installing from
      # requirements.txt is the version that cannot drift again: it is the
      # same file the app itself installs from, pinned the same way.
      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: pip install -r requirements.txt

      # Every day this does not run is a day of replay history that cannot be
      # recovered later. Deliberately the cheapest and most frequent job.
      - name: Nightly Bootstrap Archive
        if: (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.step == 'archive') || github.event.schedule == '0 2 * * *'
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.DATABASE_URL }}
        run: python scripts/archive_bootstrap.py

      # NB: snapshot_xp.py opens with DELETE FROM fpl_predictions WHERE
      # gameweek = %s. Previously every step ran on any workflow_dispatch, so a
      # manual run mid-gameweek deleted that gameweek's predictions and
      # destroyed their pairing with the actuals already ingested. The step
      # input above makes each step individually selectable.
      - name: Friday Snapshot
        if: (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.step == 'snapshot') || github.event.schedule == '0 16 * * 5'
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.DATABASE_URL }}
        run: python scripts/snapshot_xp.py

      - name: Tuesday Ingest Actuals
        if: (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.step == 'ingest') || github.event.schedule == '0 10 * * 2'
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.DATABASE_URL }}
        run: python scripts/ingest_actuals.py

      # Re-enabled. The four Stage 8 calibration repairs (damping, the frozen
      # dc_sensitivity gradient, the surrogate mismatch, the loss floor) had
      # already landed; what was still missing was point-in-time integrity in
      # the training archive, which fpl_tools._team_attack_def_ratings'
      # `as_of_event` now enforces and ARITH_FINGERPRINT now stamps.
      #
      # The Wednesday cron was declared in `on.schedule` but NOT named in this
      # step's `if:`, so a scheduled run fired the workflow and matched no
      # step at all -- auto-tune had effectively never run on a schedule, only
      # by hand. Both triggers are named explicitly now so the two cannot
      # drift apart again.
      #
      # FPL_AUTOTUNE_ENABLED is set HERE rather than defaulted ON in
      # scripts/auto_tune.py on purpose. The job writes weights.json into the
      # repo and auto-commits it below, so the opt-in belongs at the one call
      # site that is meant to do that. The script stays inert by default, and
      # a stray `python scripts/auto_tune.py` -- or a future caller that
      # forgets to check ENABLED -- cannot silently rewrite production
      # weights. AutoTuneGuardTest holds that default in place.
      - name: Wednesday Auto-Tune & Commit
        if: (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.step == 'autotune') || github.event.schedule == '0 10 * * 3'
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.DATABASE_URL }}
          FPL_AUTOTUNE_ENABLED: "1"
        run: |
          python scripts/auto_tune.py
          git config --global user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
          git config --global user.email 'github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
          git add weights.json
          git diff --quiet && git diff --staged --quiet || (git commit -m "Auto-tune: Recalibrated baseline weights" && git push)
```

### `.github/workflows/tests.yml`

_58 lines_

```yaml
name: Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 3 * * *'   # nightly full golden-file suite

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'

      # Installs from requirements.txt rather than a hand-maintained package
      # list. The list used to be typed out here directly (requests pulp numpy
      # python-dateutil pytest) and never included streamlit -- so every test
      # that actually executes app.py (render_app.py, probe_ui.py; both
      # `import streamlit` at module scope) failed with ModuleNotFoundError on
      # every push since this workflow existed. It never surfaced locally
      # because streamlit was already installed in the dev environment, and
      # nobody had looked at the Actions tab. requirements.txt is the pinned
      # single source of truth (Stage 8a); reading from it means this list
      # cannot drift out of sync with the app's real dependencies again.
      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: pip install -r requirements.txt pytest

      # Scope split. 20 squads x 4 solve paths is 80 MILP solves, and the
      # deterministic profile allows each up to 60s -- a worst case no one wants
      # blocking a pull request. Per-commit runs the 5-squad smoke set (both
      # formation traps included, so the Stage 1 gate keeps its teeth); the
      # nightly run does all 20.
      - name: Select golden-file scope
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "schedule" ]; then
            echo "FPL_GOLDEN_SCOPE=full" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          else
            echo "FPL_GOLDEN_SCOPE=smoke" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      # Solves must prove optimality here. A wall-clock-limited incumbent varies
      # with runner load, which would make the golden files flap.
      - name: Run tests
        env:
          FPL_SOLVER_PROFILE: deterministic
        run: python -m pytest tests/ -q

      # The committed fixture must be exactly what the generator produces --
      # a hand-edited fixture would make every golden file unreproducible.
      - name: Verify fixture is reproducible
        run: |
          python tests/fixtures/build_bootstrap.py
          git diff --exit-code -- tests/fixtures/
```

```css
/* FPL Quant Manager -- single stylesheet.
 *
 * Replaces five separate <style> blocks (CSS, DARK_CSS, DARK_CSS2, DARK_CSS3,
 * DARK_CSS4) injected in sequence. That arrangement had three problems:
 *
 *   - .streamlit/config.toml forces base = "dark", so the entire light block
 *     was dead weight for every class the dark blocks redefined -- while ten
 *     classes styled ONLY in the light block still rendered light-on-dark.
 *   - Selectors were redefined across blocks with different values
 *     (.pitch-player 92px then 96px, .headshot 44x56 then 65x85), so the
 *     result depended on injection order rather than on intent.
 *   - Every colour was a hex literal, repeated across blocks and scattered
 *     through ~25 inline f-strings, with two greens and two reds expressing
 *     the same semantic.
 *
 * Generated by collapsing that cascade, so the rendered design is unchanged;
 * colours are now tokens. Edit this file, not app.py.
 */

:root {
  --bg:        #0B1320;   /* page */
  --surface:   #1E293B;   /* cards */
  --surface-2: #0F172A;   /* inset panels */
  --line:      #334155;   /* borders */
  --text:      #E2E8F0;
  --text-2:    #CBD5E1;
  --muted:     #94A3B8;
  --muted-2:   #64748B;
  --pos:       #00F5A0;   /* the single positive/accent colour */
  --pos-2:     #10B981;
  --neg:       #F43F5E;   /* the single negative colour */
  --neg-2:     #EF4444;
  --neg-soft:  #FDA4AF;
  --warn:      #FBBF24;
  /* Text on a saturated position chip. A literal #fff was the last hardcoded
     hex outside this block, which is the one thing the Stage 7 gate forbids. */
  --on-chip:   #FFFFFF;
  /* Status tints: success / danger / warning / info surfaces and their
     foregrounds. Previously 19 loose hex literals doing semantic work. */
  --pos-bg:    #0F2B20;  --pos-bg-2:  #113824;  --pos-bg-3: #0B2418;
  --pos-fg:    #BBF7D0;  --pos-line:  #16A34A;
  --neg-bg:    #3B1220;  --neg-line:  #7F1D1D;  --neg-line-2: #E11D48;
  --neg-fg:    #FECDD3;  --neg-fg-2:  #FECACA;
  --warn-bg:   #3B2F12;  --warn-line: #92400E;  --warn-2:   #F59E0B;
  --warn-fg:   #FDE68A;  --warn-fg-2: #FED7AA;
  --info:      #4F46E5;  --info-2:    #38BDF8;  --info-fg:  #E0E7FF;
  --line-2:    #475569;

  --r:         12px;
  --pad:       16px;
}

#MainMenu, footer {visibility: hidden;}
/* Safety net: the page itself must never scroll sideways. Only one narrow
   media query (max-width:768px) existed before this, scoped to the pitch
   view alone -- every other wide row (the Model Health table's fixed-width
   stat columns, the transfer-pair layout) had nothing stopping it pushing
   past a phone's viewport, which is what "cut off outside the frame" is:
   content shoved past the right edge with no scrollbar to reach it. This
   clips that possibility at the root; the specific offenders below also get
   their own overflow-x:auto so their content stays reachable by a contained
   swipe rather than merely being hidden. */
.block-container {padding-top: 1.4rem; padding-bottom: 4rem; max-width: 1240px; color: var(--text); overflow-x: hidden;}

/* Safety net: no card should ever grow its OWN vertical scrollbar. Streamlit
   gives several of its own container primitives a default max-height once
   their content is tall enough (a bordered container, an expander body, a
   metric row sitting inside one) -- which reads as a second, nested scroll
   region inside a page that already scrolls, e.g. under "How your squad
   stacks up" in Step 4. The page itself is the one place that should ever
   scroll vertically; every card sizes to its content instead. */
[data-testid="stVerticalBlock"] > div:has(div[data-testid="stMetric"]),
.stCard,
div[data-testid="stExpander"],
div[data-testid="stVerticalBlockBorderWrapper"] {
    overflow-y: visible !important;
    max-height: none !important;
}
.deadline-hero {background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--text); border-left: 6px solid var(--info); border-radius: 14px; padding: 18px 22px; margin-bottom: 16px; box-shadow: none; border-color: var(--line); border-left-color: var(--pos);}
.dl-gw {font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.14em; color: var(--pos); text-transform: uppercase;}
.dl-time {font-size: 1.9rem; font-weight: 800; color: var(--text); line-height: 1.15; margin-top: 2px;}
.dl-warning {color: var(--neg-soft); font-size: 0.88rem; margin-top: 6px;}
.overview {background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--info-fg); border-radius: 14px; padding: 16px 20px; color: var(--text-2); font-size: 0.94rem; line-height: 1.55; margin-bottom: 8px; border-color: var(--line);}
.overview b {color: var(--pos);}
.card {background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--text); border-radius: 14px; padding: 18px 20px; margin-bottom: 14px; box-shadow: 0 4px 14px rgba(0,0,0,0.25); border-color: var(--line);}
.card h3 {margin: 0 0 2px 0; font-size: 1.02rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--text);}
.section-label {text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; font-size: 0.7rem; color: var(--pos); margin-bottom: 10px;}
.grid {display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(178px, 1fr)); gap: 10px;}
.pc {border: 1px solid var(--text); border-radius: 12px; padding: 12px 13px; background: var(--surface-2); border-color: var(--line);}
.pc .pos {display: inline-block; font-size: 0.66rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.05em; padding: 2px 7px; border-radius: 5px; color: var(--on-chip);}
.pc .nm {font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.92rem; margin: 6px 0 1px 0; color: var(--text);}
.pc .meta {color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.75rem;}
.bar {height: 5px; background: var(--line); border-radius: 3px; margin: 8px 0 4px 0; overflow: hidden;}
.bar-fill {height: 100%; border-radius: 3px;}
.xp {font-weight: 800; font-size: 0.88rem;}
.badge {display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 8px 13px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--info-fg); font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--pos); border-color: var(--line);}
.badge .g {width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--pos); box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--pos);}
.cap-card {border: 1px solid var(--warn); background: var(--pos-bg); border-color: var(--pos);}
.role {display: inline-block; font-size: 0.62rem; font-weight: 800; padding: 1px 6px; border-radius: 5px; margin-left: 5px; vertical-align: middle;}
.role-c {background: var(--pos); color: var(--bg);}
.role-vc {background: var(--line); color: var(--text-2);}
.stat-badge {display: inline-block; font-size: 0.6rem; font-weight: 700; padding: 1px 5px; border-radius: 4px; margin-left: 4px; white-space: nowrap; vertical-align: middle;}
.stat-out {background: var(--neg-bg); color: var(--neg-soft); border: 1px solid var(--neg-fg-2); border-color: var(--neg-line);}
.stat-doubt {background: var(--warn-bg); color: var(--warn); border: 1px solid var(--warn-fg); border-color: var(--warn-line);}
.chip-banner {background: var(--pos-bg); border: 1px solid var(--pos-fg); border-left: 5px solid var(--pos-line); border-radius: 10px; padding: 12px 16px; margin-bottom: 12px; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--pos-fg); border-color: var(--pos-line); border-left-color: var(--pos);}
.override-head {background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--warn-fg-2); border-left: 6px solid var(--warn-2); border-radius: 14px 14px 0 0; padding: 16px 20px; font-size: 1.15rem; font-weight: 800; color: var(--text); margin-top: 26px; border-color: var(--line); border-left-color: var(--pos);}
.override-head span {color: var(--pos); font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 600; margin-left: 8px;}
.dummy-url {display: inline-block; background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px dashed var(--text-2); border-radius: 6px; padding: 2px 8px; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.78rem; color: var(--muted); margin-left: 6px; border-color: var(--line);}
.team-row {display: flex; gap: 12px; align-items: stretch; margin-bottom: 10px;}
.pos-col {flex: 0 0 64px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: var(--surface-2); border-radius: 10px; padding: 8px; border-color: var(--line);}
.pos-emoji {font-size: 1.3rem;}
.pos-name {font-weight: 800; font-size: 0.68rem; letter-spacing: .06em; color: var(--muted); margin-top: 2px;}
.starters {flex: 1; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill,minmax(148px,1fr)); gap: 8px; align-content: start;}
.subs {flex: 0 0 205px; background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px dashed var(--text-2); border-radius: 10px; padding: 8px 10px; border-color: var(--line);}
.sub-title {font-size: 0.62rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); margin-bottom: 4px;}
.sub-item {font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--text); font-weight: 600; padding: 4px 0; border-bottom: 1px dotted var(--text); display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; gap: 4px; border-bottom-color: var(--line);}
.sub-item:last-child {border-bottom: none;}
.sub-meta {color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.68rem; margin-top: 2px;}
.sub-xp {color: var(--pos); font-weight: 800; white-space: nowrap; margin-top: 2px;}
.empty {color: var(--line-2); font-size: 0.8rem;}
.mc {border: 1px solid var(--text); border-left: 3px solid var(--muted); border-radius: 10px; padding: 8px 10px; background: var(--surface-2); min-width: 0; border-color: var(--line);}
.mc .pos {display: inline-block; font-size: 0.6rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.04em; padding: 1px 6px; border-radius: 4px; color: var(--bg); vertical-align: middle;}
.mc-nm {font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.82rem; color: var(--text); margin-top: 4px; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;}
.mc-meta {color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.7rem; margin-top: 2px;}
.mc-xp {font-weight: 800; font-size: 0.8rem; margin-top: 3px; color: var(--pos);}
.alert-box {background: var(--neg-bg); border: 1px solid var(--neg-fg); border-left: 4px solid var(--neg-line-2); padding: 12px 16px; border-radius: 8px; margin: 10px 0; border-color: var(--neg-line); border-left-color: var(--neg-soft); color: var(--neg-fg);}
.stApp {background: var(--bg);}
[data-testid="stSidebar"] {background: var(--surface-2); border-right: 1px solid var(--line);}
[data-testid="stSidebar"] * {color: var(--text);}

/* Pin the sidebar open on desktop -- Streamlit's own collapse control (the
   "<<" arrow) let a desktop user accidentally hide the Strategy & Chip
   controls with one misclick, with no obvious way back short of finding the
   arrow again. Scoped to >=992px so mobile/tablet keep Streamlit's own
   collapse-to-hamburger behaviour, which is exactly where a narrow viewport
   needs the screen space back. */
@media (min-width: 992px) {
    [data-testid="stSidebarCollapseButton"] {display: none !important;}
    [data-testid="stSidebar"] {
        min-width: 300px !important;
        max-width: 320px !important;
        transform: none !important;
        visibility: visible !important;
    }
}
[data-testid="stHeader"] {background: rgba(11,19,32,0.5);}
.headshot {width: 44px; height: 56px; object-fit: cover; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--line);}
.pitch {background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--pos-bg-2) 0%, var(--pos-bg-3) 100%); border: 2px solid var(--line); border-radius: 16px; padding: 20px 16px; margin-bottom: 14px;}
.pitch-row {display: flex; justify-content: space-around; align-items: center; margin: 14px 0;}
.pitch-player {text-align: center; width: 92px;}
.pitch-player .nm {font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--text); margin-top: 4px; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; width: 100%;}
.pitch-player .meta {font-size: 0.68rem; color: var(--muted); width: 100%; white-space: nowrap;}
.pitch-player .xp {font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 800; color: var(--pos);}
.dugout {background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px dashed var(--line); border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px 16px; margin-bottom: 14px;}
.dugout-title {font-size: 0.62rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted-2); margin-bottom: 10px;}
.transfer-pair {display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px;}
/* min-width:0 is load-bearing: without it a flex:1 child still refuses to
   shrink below its CONTENT's natural width (a long name plus "MID · Newcastle
   United · £6.5m" easily runs 180px+), so two of these plus the arrow plus the
   fixed xP/cost block genuinely could not fit a phone's content width and had
   nothing to give -- the row just overflowed the page. */
.transfer-card {flex: 1; min-width: 0; border-radius: 12px; padding: 12px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--line); background: var(--surface-2);}
.transfer-card.tc-out {border-left: 4px solid var(--neg);}
.transfer-card.tc-in {border-left: 4px solid var(--pos);}
.transfer-arrow {font-size: 1.4rem; color: var(--pos); font-weight: 800; flex-shrink: 0;}
.tc-name {font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;}
.tc-meta {font-size: 0.72rem; color: var(--muted); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;}
.rot-card {background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px 16px; margin-bottom: 10px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px;}
.rot-score {font-size: 1.1rem; font-weight: 800; color: var(--pos); min-width: 54px;}
.fdr-strip {display: flex; gap: 4px; margin-top: 8px;}
.fdr-cell {width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 6px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 800; color: var(--bg);}
.strength-card {background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px 16px; margin-bottom: 10px;}
.strength-bar {height: 6px; background: var(--line); border-radius: 3px; overflow: hidden; margin: 4px 0;}
.strength-fill-home {height: 100%; background: var(--info-2);}
.strength-fill-away {height: 100%; background: var(--pos);}
.momentum-row {display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 10px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);}
.momentum-row:last-child {border-bottom: none;}
.momentum-badge-up {background: var(--pos-bg); color: var(--pos); border: 1px solid var(--pos-line); padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 800; white-space: nowrap;}
.momentum-badge-down {background: var(--neg-bg); color: var(--neg-soft); border: 1px solid var(--neg-line); padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 800; white-space: nowrap;}
.radar-card {background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 12px; padding: 12px 14px;}
.radar-card .nm {font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--text);}
.radar-card .meta {color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.7rem;}
/* Player-market card (.pmc): a unified grid so name/position-price/fixture-
   dots and xP never drift relative to each other. Built with CSS Grid even
   on desktop -- photo spans both rows on the left, info stacks in row 1,
   xP sits under it in row 2 -- specifically so it reproduces today's exact
   visual arrangement (this is not a new desktop look, just the old flex
   layout expressed as grid), which makes the mobile-only re-flow to a
   single 48px/1fr/auto row (see the 600px block) a pure grid-template
   change with no markup difference between breakpoints. */
.pmc {display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; grid-template-rows: auto auto; column-gap: 8px;}
.pmc-photo {grid-column: 1; grid-row: 1 / 3; flex-shrink: 0;}
.pmc-info {grid-column: 2; grid-row: 1; min-width: 0;}
.pmc-xp {grid-column: 2; grid-row: 2; font-weight: 800; color: var(--pos); margin-top: 4px;}
.cap-pill {background: var(--pos); color: var(--bg); font-weight: 800; font-size: 0.6rem; padding: 1px 5px; border-radius: 4px;}
.photo-frame {position: relative; display: inline-block; line-height: 0;}
.photo-frame .badge-overlay {position: absolute; right: -3px; bottom: -3px; line-height: 0;}
.photo-frame .badge-overlay .badge-img {width: 18px; height: 18px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--bg); border: 1px solid var(--bg);}
/* Club crest fallback: a styled div (background-image), never a bare <img>
   -- same reasoning as .headshot. An unmapped team (no `code` at all) has
   no image attempt to fail, so it renders its short-name initials as a
   genuine, permanent fallback rather than the silent gap this used to
   leave; a real crest that 404s at runtime falls back to this class's own
   solid surface colour, same as every other image on the page. */
.badge-crest {display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 50%; background-color: var(--surface-2); color: var(--muted); font-weight: 800; vertical-align: middle; flex-shrink: 0;}
.badge-crest.badge-img {width: 16px; height: 16px; font-size: 0.5rem;}
.badge-crest.badge-lg {width: 28px; height: 28px; font-size: 0.62rem;}
/* Pitch player cards: strict fixed dimensions so a 404 fallback never collapses the grid. */ .pitch-player {display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 3px; text-align: center; width: 96px;}
.pitch-player .photo-frame {width: 65px; height: 85px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;}
.pitch-player .headshot {width: 65px; height: 85px; object-fit: cover; border-radius: 8px; display: block;}
/* Fixture-difficulty dots: real, precisely-sized circular elements, not
   emoji glyphs -- an emoji's rendered size follows font-size and the
   platform's own emoji font, which CSS width/height cannot touch, so on a
   crowded mobile pitch card there was no reliable way to shrink or bound
   them. A dedicated flex container keeps all four bound to their own
   player's card and centred, so they can never visually collide into a
   neighbouring card. */
.fx-dots {display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; gap: 3px; margin-top: 2px;}
.fx-dot {display: inline-block; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--muted-2); flex-shrink: 0;}
.fx-dot-green {background: var(--pos);}
.fx-dot-amber {background: var(--warn);}
.fx-dot-red {background: var(--neg);}
.fx-dot-double {background: var(--info-2);}
.fx-dot-blank {background: var(--muted-2); opacity: 0.5;}
/* Pitch row position labels */ .pitch-row {display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; margin: 14px 0;}
.pitch-row-label {flex: 0 0 34px; font-size: 0.62rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-align: center; text-transform: uppercase;}
.pitch-row-cards {flex: 1; display: flex; justify-content: space-around; align-items: center; gap: 8px;}
.tc-head {display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;}
/* The headshot must never shrink; the name/meta column next to it must be
   ALLOWED to, or .tc-name/.tc-meta's ellipsis rules have no narrower box to
   ellipsis into -- text-overflow only fires once the box itself is already
   constrained below the text's natural width. */
.tc-head .photo-frame {flex-shrink: 0;}
.tc-head > div:last-child {min-width: 0; overflow: hidden;}
/* Fixture-run track under each "The move" player card: 4 fixtures, one
   circular FDR badge + opponent/venue + that gameweek's xP per cell. Sits
   inside .transfer-card, so the two tracks are already flex siblings via
   .transfer-pair and line up side-by-side automatically. */
.fx-run {display: flex; flex-direction: row; justify-content: space-between; gap: 4px; margin-top: 10px; padding-top: 8px; border-top: 1px solid var(--line);}
.fx-run-cell {flex: 1; min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 2px;}
.fx-run-badge {width: 24px; height: 24px; border-radius: 50%; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 800; color: var(--bg); flex-shrink: 0;}
.fx-run-badge.fx-run-blank {background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--muted); border: 1px dashed var(--line);}
.fx-run-opp {font-size: 0.6rem; color: var(--muted); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; max-width: 100%;}
.fx-run-xp {font-size: 0.66rem; color: var(--text); font-weight: 700; white-space: nowrap;}
/* Player Inspector */ .inspector-card {background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 14px; padding: 16px 18px; margin-top: 4px;}
.insp-fixture {display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; padding: 7px 0; border-bottom: 1px dotted var(--line);}
.insp-fixture:last-child {border-bottom: none;}
/* Was repeat(5, 1fr): a hard 5-column grid with no minmax floor, so on a
   phone each track was forced below what a 132px label plus a bar plus a
   value can hold -- and a fixed track count has nowhere to reflow to, so it
   just overflowed, cutting off MID/FWD/Bench and truncating their text.
   auto-fit/minmax is the same idiom already used for .grid, .scorecard and
   .mh-grid elsewhere in this file: 200px keeps 5 across on a normal desktop
   width (5*200 + 4 gaps fits inside the .card's ~1136px content width) while
   wrapping to fewer columns, then one full-width column, as the viewport
   narrows -- no separate media query needed. */
.signal-grid {display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)); gap: 10px;}
.signal-card {background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 12px; padding: 12px 14px;}
.signal-head {display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; margin-bottom: 10px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--text);}
.signal-score {margin-left: auto; font-size: 1.15rem; font-weight: 800; color: var(--pos);}
.signal-delta {font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; margin-left: 4px;}
.signal-row {display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; margin: 5px 0;}
.signal-label {flex: 0 0 132px; font-size: 0.66rem; color: var(--muted); letter-spacing: 0.02em;}
.signal-bar {flex: 1; height: 5px; background: var(--line); border-radius: 3px; overflow: hidden;}
.signal-fill {height: 100%; border-radius: 3px;}
.signal-val {flex: 0 0 22px; font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 700; text-align: right;}

/* Responsive overrides, carried over verbatim. */
@media (max-width: 768px) {
    .pitch { padding: 12px 6px !important; }
    .pitch-row-label { display: none !important; }
    .pitch-row-cards { width: 100% !important; gap: 2px !important; justify-content: space-evenly !important; }
    .pitch-player { width: auto !important; flex: 1 1 0 !important; max-width: 20% !important; min-width: 0 !important; padding: 2px !important; gap: 1px !important; }
    .pitch-player .photo-frame, .pitch-player .headshot { display: none !important; }
    .pitch-player .nm { font-size: 0.65rem !important; }
    .pitch-player .meta { font-size: 0.58rem !important; }
    .pitch-player .fx-dot { width: 8px !important; height: 8px !important; }
    .dugout { padding: 10px 8px !important; }
    .dugout > div:last-child { gap: 4px !important; justify-content: space-evenly !important; }
  }

/* Below 768px, forcing every row into one strict line (max-width:20% per
   card, all five in the widest MID/DEF rows squeezed side by side) is what
   overcrowded and truncated the cards on a genuinely narrow phone: a 5-man
   line got ~70px per player -- not enough for a name, price/xP AND a row of
   fixture dots without them running into the neighbouring card. Below
   600px, cards wrap into a staggered layout instead (three per row, so a
   5-man line reads as 3+2 and a back-4 gets real width on its own three-per-
   row grid), each gets an explicit bounded surface so it is visually
   obvious which name/price/dots belong together, and text/dots are tuned
   down to fit that surface. This block also covers the two other narrow-
   viewport fixes bundled with the same pass: "The move" card's transfer
   pair stacking vertically instead of squeezing two cards side by side, and
   the player-market card grid re-flowing to a single 48px/1fr/auto row.
   All of it additive to the 768px block above and must come after it in
   the file -- both match below 600px, and later !important rules win the
   tie on shared selectors. Desktop (>=600px) is untouched: nothing here is
   reachable above this breakpoint. */
@media (max-width: 600px) {
    .pitch-row-cards { flex-wrap: wrap !important; justify-content: center !important; gap: 6px 4px !important; }
    .pitch-player {
        flex: 0 1 30% !important;
        max-width: 30% !important;
        background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.7) !important;
        border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08) !important;
        border-radius: 6px !important;
        padding: 4px 3px !important;
    }
    .pitch-player .nm { font-size: 0.70rem !important; line-height: 1.1 !important; text-overflow: ellipsis !important; }
    .pitch-player .meta { font-size: 0.65rem !important; }
    .pitch-player .fx-dot { width: 7px !important; height: 7px !important; margin: 0 1px !important; }
    .dugout > div:last-child { justify-content: center !important; }

    /* "The move" card (Step 3): side-by-side Transfer Out/In no longer fits
       below 600px without truncating names and colliding the two 4-fixture
       tracks -- stacked full-width, each card gets real room and the
       fixture badges (below) have no neighbouring card left to collide
       into. */
    .transfer-pair { flex-direction: column !important; align-items: stretch !important; gap: 8px !important; }
    .transfer-card { width: 100% !important; max-width: 100% !important; }
    .transfer-arrow { align-self: center !important; transform: rotate(90deg) !important; }
    .tc-score { min-width: 0 !important; width: 100% !important; text-align: center !important; display: flex !important; align-items: center !important; justify-content: center !important; gap: 8px !important; }

    /* The fixture track was already flex/row/space-between with each cell
       flex:1;min-width:0 (see .fx-run-cell) -- a full-width stacked card
       gives that row enough room on its own; nothing further needed here. */

    /* Player-market cards (.pmc: Radar Shortlists): re-flow the same three
       pieces (photo/info/xp) from the two-row desktop grid into the
       requested single-row 48px/1fr/auto -- no markup difference between
       breakpoints, only which grid cells they're placed in. */
    .pmc { grid-template-columns: 48px 1fr auto !important; grid-template-rows: auto !important; column-gap: 8px !important; align-items: center !important; }
    .pmc-photo { grid-row: 1 !important; grid-column: 1 !important; }
    .pmc-info { grid-row: 1 !important; grid-column: 2 !important; }
    .pmc-xp { grid-row: 1 !important; grid-column: 3 !important; margin-top: 0 !important; white-space: nowrap; }
}
.note{font-size:0.78rem;color:var(--muted-2);margin:6px 0 10px 0;}
.note-inline{font-size:0.8rem;color:var(--muted);}

/* Objective waterfall: the decomposition the solver actually maximised. Also
   the Model Health week-by-week table -- same row shape, same fixed-width
   numeric columns. Three min-width columns plus a label routinely exceed a
   phone's content width (label ~130px + 3x70-80px + gaps easily tops 380px
   against ~340px of actual room), so this scrolls within itself on a narrow
   screen rather than pushing the page or losing its right-hand columns to
   the page-level overflow clip. */
.wf{margin:10px 0 4px 0;border-top:1px solid var(--line);padding-top:8px;
    overflow-x:auto;}
.wf-row{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:12px;padding:3px 0;
        font-size:0.82rem;color:var(--text-2);width:max-content;min-width:100%;}
.wf-net{border-top:1px solid var(--line);margin-top:6px;padding-top:6px;
        font-weight:700;color:var(--text);}
.wf-warn{margin-top:8px;font-size:0.78rem;color:var(--warn-fg);
         background:var(--warn-bg);border:1px solid var(--warn-line);
         border-radius:8px;padding:8px 10px;}

/* Squad scorecard: how the squad is built, not what it scored. */
.scorecard{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(160px,1fr));
           gap:10px;margin:4px 0 2px 0;}
.sc-tile{background:var(--surface-2);border:1px solid var(--line);
         border-radius:var(--r);padding:12px 14px;}
.sc-label{font-size:0.74rem;color:var(--muted);font-weight:600;
          letter-spacing:0.02em;margin-bottom:4px;}
.sc-value{font-size:1.5rem;font-weight:800;color:var(--text);line-height:1.15;}
.sc-of{font-size:0.95rem;font-weight:600;color:var(--muted-2);}
.sc-sub{font-size:0.74rem;color:var(--muted-2);margin-top:3px;}
.sc-takers{font-size:0.72rem;color:var(--muted);margin-top:3px;line-height:1.4;}

/* Model Health: the scorecard the hero copy promises. */
.mh-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(180px,1fr));gap:10px;}
.mh-bar{height:8px;border-radius:4px;background:var(--surface-2);
        border:1px solid var(--line);overflow:hidden;margin-top:8px;}
.mh-bar > div{height:100%;background:var(--pos-2);}
```
